title: Synapse-specific reconsolidation of distinct fear memories in the lateral amygdala
protocol: Implant rats with LA cannulas and a stimulation electrode aimed at the left auditory thalamus.
Attach an insulated stainless steel recording wire to the left LA cannula, extending approximately 0.5 mm from the base of the infusion cannula.
Determine the final depth using stimulation of the MGm/PIN as a guide.
Place two cortical silver balls contralaterally to serve as a reference and ground.
Leave animals at least one week before starting the experiment.
Choose two CSs, either made of pure tone or FM tone, to minimize generalization.
Use a 20-s series of acoustic tone pips for the pure tone CS \(1 kHz, 50-ms duration, 1-ms ramp, intensity 20 dB higher than background noise, delivered at 1 Hz).

Use a 20-s series of frequency modulation tone sweeps for the FM tone CS \(12.5-kHz carrier frequency, 50-Hz modulation frequency, 2.5-kHz modulation depth, 250-ms duration, 1-ms ramp, intensity 20 dB higher than background noise, delivered at 1 Hz).
Reactivate one of the tones in a counterbalanced manner in each experiment.
Use a 0.5-s \(0.75-mA) electric foot shock as the US.
Place rats in the conditioning chamber for 30 min on two consecutive days.

Give rats three pre-exposures of one CS followed by three pre-exposures of another CS in the chamber with a variable intertrial interval of approximately 157 seconds, reversing the order on the next day.
Place the rats in the chamber and allow them to acclimate for 120 seconds.
Present three CSr-US pairings and three CSn-US pairings in the chamber with a variable intertrial interval of approximately 130 seconds, delivering the US immediately after each CS ends.
Acclimate the rats to the modified context chamber for 120 seconds before presenting a single CSr.
Thirty minutes prior to reactivation, infuse rats bilaterally with U0126 (1 μg; 0.5 μl in 50% DMSO) or an equivalent volume of vehicle (50% DMSO).
Place rats in the chamber three hours after the reactivation trial.
Allow acclimation for 120 seconds.
Present four presentations of CSr.
Wait 180 seconds after the CSr presentations.
Present four presentations of CSn.
Approximately 24 hours after the reactivation trial, conduct a PR-LTM test.
Present nine CSr.
Present nine CSn in the same order as the PR-STM test.
Record rats' freezing behavior onto videotape during all sessions for off-line scoring.
Record auditory-evoked field potentials \(AEFPs\) from both the LA and MGm/PIN through the tip of the stimulation electrode.
Analyze AEFP recordings using DataWave software.
Average AEFPs across all tone-pip presentations within a trial and collapse data across trials.
Measure the amplitude of the short latency negative component for each potential: 12-16 ms for the LA, 7-9 ms for the MGm/PIN.
Express retention of behavioral and electrophysiological changes as a percentage during the last four trials of the PR-LTM test relative to the four trials of the PR-STM test.
